findings.title: "Web-parity-lite" scope is actually near-full web parity
findings.evidence: Problem Frame says mobile is needed for 'pipeline status, recent activities, overdue invoices, and clock-in records.' Requirements R2-R7 and implementation units U5-U10 cover dashboard, deals, contacts, companies, activities, invoices, and HR. Scope boundaries list only public store submission, push notifications, offline sync, deep linking, storefront, and admin/permission UI as out of scope. This is not a 'lite' Phase 1; it is a port of nearly every web module.
findings.suggested_fix: Define a true MVP with no more than 3 modules (e.g., auth + dashboard + activities quick-add). Move contacts/companies, invoices, and HR to Phase 2 unless a specific mobile job-to-be-done justifies each. Add a hard scope gate after MVP validation.

findings.title: Auth integration risk is treated as a spike-within-implementation rather than a pre-commit gate
findings.evidence: Risks table lists 'Better Auth mobile session sharing is non-trivial' as Medium/High with mitigation 'Spike in U3 before building screens; fallback to webview login if needed.' However, U3 is titled 'Set up mobile auth and Convex provider' and includes full login screen, providers, and navigation integration. Open Questions also defer 'Exact Better Auth token exchange mechanism for mobile vs web session sharing.' Webview login would undermine the native UX justification in the Overview.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a dedicated U0 proof-of-concept spike that proves Better Auth session/token exchange works in a React Native bundle against the existing backend. Define explicit go/no-go criteria before U3 is approved. If the spike fails, reconsider PWA/responsive-web or a simpler API-token auth path instead of a webview fallback.

findings.title: Shared-package refactor is bigger than the plan assumes
findings.evidence: `packages/auth/src/index.ts` and `packages/config/src/index.ts` are currently empty. Web `env.ts` uses `@t3-oss/env-nextjs` which is Next.js-specific. `apps/web/src/lib/convex/hooks/convex-hooks.ts` imports `sonner` (a web-only toast library) and `@/lib/convex/components/convex-provider` (a web-specific React component). U2 only gives a few files and an 'execution note' to start with a failing typecheck.
findings.suggested_fix: Before extracting, audit all shared hooks/helpers for web-only imports (Next.js, sonner, react-dom, browser-only APIs). Create platform-agnostic notification/error interfaces in `@crm/utils` or `@crm/ui-core` so mobile can substitute native toasts. Add a migration unit specifically for decoupling shared code from web-specific providers.

findings.title: Navigation library is deferred despite being load-bearing for file structure
findings.evidence: Open Questions defer 'Final navigation library choice (React Navigation vs Expo Router) after spike.' Meanwhile U1 creates `app/(app)/deals/[id].tsx`, `app/(app)/activities/new.tsx`, etc. — a file structure that only makes sense for Expo Router. React Navigation would use a different structure with `src/navigation/` and imperative screens.
findings.suggested_fix: Resolve the navigation choice in a pre-U1 spike or make U1 explicitly conditional on Expo Router. If React Navigation is chosen, rewrite the Output Structure section to use `src/navigation` and screen components rather than `app/` file-based routes. Do not create screen files until the navigation model is fixed.

findings.title: Push notifications deferred while listed as a core benefit
findings.evidence: Overview states a native mobile app provides 'faster input, better notification support, and a UX tailored to small screens.' Scope Boundaries explicitly list 'push notifications' as out of scope and defer them to follow-up work. This creates a justification gap: one of the three stated benefits is not delivered in Phase 1.
findings.suggested_fix: Either (a) include a minimal notification MVP in Phase 1 (e.g., local reminders for overdue activities), or (b) remove 'better notification support' from the problem justification and reframe the value around offline speed and mobile-optimized input instead.

findings.title: No evidence that the responsive web experience is inadequate
findings.evidence: Problem Frame says 'The CRM currently only has a desktop web experience.' This frames the absence of a native app as the problem, but does not establish that the existing web app is unusable on mobile or that users actually need native features. Context & Research has no user research, analytics, or support tickets cited.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a baseline validation step: review mobile web usage analytics, run a short user interview with 2-3 field sales reps, or prototype a mobile-optimized web dashboard to compare against the cost of native development. Document the evidence that native is necessary before committing to the build.

findings.title: Dashboard-first layout may not match mobile jobs-to-be-done
findings.evidence: R2 prioritizes 'dashboard KPIs and insights on app launch' and U5 builds KPI cards, insights widget, charts, and recent activities. The Problem Frame, however, emphasizes on-the-go access to pipeline status, activities, invoices, and clock-in. Mobile users typically need quick capture and lookup more than analytics browsing.
findings.suggested_fix: Validate mobile workflows before finalizing the home screen. Consider making the primary entry point a quick-action FAB or an activities list, with dashboard as a secondary tab. Add a user-journey spike to the plan with concrete findings.

findings.title: Online-only Phase 1 assumes reliable connectivity for field users
findings.evidence: Key Technical Decisions table states 'Online-only Phase 1' with rationale 'Offline sync adds significant complexity; optimistic UI with network feedback is sufficient for first release.' The Problem Frame explicitly mentions 'field staff' as users. Field staff often operate in low-connectivity environments.
findings.suggested_fix: Document the connectivity assumption explicitly and validate it with the target user group. Even without full offline sync, add read-through cache, request queuing for mutations, and clear offline/error states so the app degrades gracefully rather than showing blank screens.

findings.title: Internal distribution is not as lightweight as the plan implies
findings.evidence: U11 'Set up internal distribution builds' lists TestFlight and APK as the final step. EAS Build + TestFlight still requires an Apple Developer Program membership ($99/year), app signing certificates, provisioning profiles, and Google Play Console setup. The verification step says 'TestFlight build is distributed to internal testers' as if it is routine.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a distribution prerequisites checklist (Apple/Google accounts, team members as testers, EAS secrets) to U11 or an earlier planning unit. Identify who owns the Apple Developer account and whether the organization already has one before implementation starts.

findings.title: HR module inclusion lacks explicit mobile justification
findings.evidence: R7 says 'Users can access HR attendance and employee list where applicable,' and U10 builds attendance and employee list. The primary personas in the Problem Frame are sales reps, field staff, and managers. HR attendance is a different use case and persona not otherwise mentioned.
findings.suggested_fix: Either remove HR from Phase 1 or add a one-paragraph justification that names the mobile HR user, their context, and why this is higher priority than other omitted modules (e.g., admin/permissions).

findings.title: No alternative to building a design system from scratch is considered
findings.evidence: U4 plans to build Button, Card, Badge, Input, Skeleton, Text, and EmptyState from React Native primitives. The plan mentions no evaluation of existing libraries (Tamagui, React Native Paper, NativeBase, Restyle) that could accelerate development.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a build-vs-use evaluation to U4. If team consistency is the priority, document why a custom system is preferred. If speed is the priority, shortlist one existing library and estimate the trade-off.

summary: The plan is internally consistent and technically plausible, but its premises are not well defended. The biggest risks are scope inflation ('web-parity-lite' is nearly a full port), auth integration treated as a spike-within-implementation, shared-package refactor scope underestimated, and the navigation model left unresolved while files are already being created. Several stated benefits (notifications, field access) are weakened by deferred or unvalidated assumptions. Before implementation, the plan needs a true MVP definition, a dedicated auth proof-of-concept, a navigation decision, and baseline evidence that native development is better than a mobile-optimized web dashboard.
